lesson.title: The Continuous & Position Verbs
lesson.subtitle: aan het werken, zitten te lezen — Dutch builds 'is doing' with a posture verb

hook.title: Dutch Has No -ing
hook.content: Dutch does not add -ing to a verb. It says aan het werken ('on the working') or uses a posture verb: zij zit te lezen, hij staat te wachten. The continuous is a small construction, not a tense.

pattern.title: Aan het + infinitive; posture + te + infinitive
pattern.content: Ik ben aan het werken, wij zijn aan het eten. With zitten/staan/liggen/lopen, Dutch adds te + infinitive: zij zit te lezen, hij staat te wachten. The posture verb adds a physical image.
pattern.linguist_note: The aan het construction is literally 'on the + infinitive'; the posture-verb construction is a Dutch speciality with no exact English equivalent.
pattern.trap_note: Do not say ik ben werkend for 'I am working'. The everyday continuous is aan het + infinitive or a posture verb.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (The Continuous & Position Verbs):
exercises.target_answer: aan, het, werken, zitten, lezen, staan
exercises.meaning: on, at; separable prefix, it; the (neuter), to work, to sit, to read, to stand
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "The Continuous & Position Verbs": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.
“Ik ben aan het werken.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “The Continuous & Position Verbs”.

cues: The pattern: Aan het + infinitive; posture + te + infinitive
exercises.explanation: “Zij zit te lezen.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Aan het + infinitive; posture + te + infinitive.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Do not say ik ben werkend for 'I am working'. The everyday continuous is aan het + infinitive or a posture verb.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Hij staat te wachten.” is word-for-word “He stands to wait.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Aan het + infinitive; posture + te + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.explanation: “Wij zijn aan het eten.” reuses only material taught in “The Continuous & Position Verbs” — Aan het + infinitive; posture + te + infinitive.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Wij zijn aan het eten.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Aan het + infinitive; posture + te + infinitive.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “She is sleeping.”
twist.explanation: Liggen ('lie') plus te + slapen pictures someone asleep; the continuous is built from the posture.

summary.outcome: Build the Dutch continuous with aan het or a posture verb + te.
summary.takeaway: Dutch 'is doing' is a picture: on the doing, or sitting/standing/lying to do.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Continuous Gym.

aan.etymology_derivation: The same preposition as English on, used in separable verbs too.

het.etymology_derivation: The neuter pronoun and article are the same little word; English split it into it and the.

werken.etymology_derivation: English work and Dutch werken are the same verb.

zitten.etymology_derivation: English sit and Dutch zitten are the same verb; s voiced to z.

lezen.etymology_derivation: English read and Dutch lezen are the same verb; the d became z in Dutch.

staan.etymology_derivation: English stand and Dutch staan are the same verb.
